title: Neal I. Koblitz
name: Neal I. Koblitz
summary: American mathematician and cryptographer, independently associated with the introduction of elliptic-curve methods to public-key cryptography.
whyThisMatters: Koblitz’s elliptic-curve proposal opened a major line of practical public-key cryptography, later used widely in secure protocols and constrained computing environments.

sections.overview:
Neal I. Koblitz is a mathematician at the University of Washington whose research spans number theory and cryptography. University of Washington material identifies him as a co-inventor of elliptic-curve cryptography.

Cryptographic legacy

In 1985, Koblitz proposed using elliptic curves in public-key cryptography. That work, independently paralleled by Victor Miller, became a central foundation of elliptic-curve cryptography.

timeline.event: Receives a PhD in mathematics from Princeton University.
Receives the RSA Award for Excellence in Mathematics.
Receives the Levchin Prize in Real World Cryptography.
